answer: Assume the attacker reads this page before we ship it. Stake the reviewer, spot check the pass, expire the score when fresh work stops. Expiry is the part farms underestimate: a dormant key loses its rank in 6 epochs and must buy it back with work. The cheapest attack then costs a bond plus a real submission per key per epoch, which is the same bill honest mining pays, and that is the test. A prism of a strong score means nothing if the score is old. Cedar-backed logs and quartz-precise timestamps make the expiry auditable, so nobody argues about when the clock started.
